Subject: FinStack — security intake and a quick scope checklist

Hi Marta — great to meet today. Thanks for the demo and the candidness on timelines. As discussed, I'm attaching our short security intake questionnaire to help us scope which systems will need evidence and what remediations might be required.

Quick recap / asks: 
- Who is the economic buyer for this initiative (name + title) so we can align procurement cadence and PO requirements?
- Which environments are in scope initially (production only, or prod + staging/dev)? Please list services or product names if possible.
- Any non-negotiable compliance items (data residency, encryption-at-rest keys you manage, third-party attestations)?
- Procurement timeline and legal redline owner so we can sync the contract milestones to your go/no-go date.

Attachments: redwood-security-questionnaire-v1.pdf (pdf) — 5 pages questionnaire with evidence checklist.

Proposed next steps: 
1) You share the completed questionnaire (or the list of systems) by EOD Friday.
2) We'll triage internally and return a scope map + evidence ask list within 48 hours.
3) Optional 30-min follow-up with Evan + our security lead if there are architecture nuances.

If it helps, I can loop in our procurement enablement lead to discuss billing and SOW cadence.

Thanks again,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the summary and the questionnaire. Quick answers inline: 

- Economic buyer: Daniel Ruiz, VP of Product (daniel.ruiz@finstack.com). He owns vendor approvals for data-platform related purchases.
- Initial scope: production only for the first phase. In-scope services: 
  - API Gateway (finstack-gw-prod)
  - Customer-facing ingestion service (ingest-prod)
  - ML inference cluster (ml-infer-prod) — will host Redwood models for our chat features
- Compliance non-negotiables: data residency in the US (no EU hosting), encryption at rest with our KMS (we manage DEKs), SOC2 type II required by onboarding, and PCI out-of-scope.
- Procurement: We'd like to close procurement in Q3. Procurement lead (cc'd) handles PO and contract redlines. Legal prefers DocuSign for signature.

I've attached our completed intake spreadsheet (high level) — still working on sample logs. Can we confirm whether Redwood requires host-based agents for log collection or if we accept syslog/API pulls?

Also tagging Evan — can you confirm what architecture diagrams you need for the security review?

Best,
Marta

Folks — forwarding Marta's responses. She identified the economic buyer (Daniel Ruiz) and production-only scope for phase 1. Procurement is in the loop.

Key asks from FinStack to address:
- Confirm hosting region: FinStack requires US-only. We need to guarantee region pinning and note any edge backups that might hit non-US regions.
- KMS integration: they manage DEKs — determine whether our offering supports customer-managed keys (we do, but need to document steps).
- Evidence: they requested SOC 2 type II; also want to see what logs we can provide and the mechanism (syslog vs agent vs API).

Proposed internal owners / quick plan: 
- Security intake triage + evidence list: Marissa (can you lead?)
- Architecture & KMS checklist: Sean (can you confirm KMS flow and region pinning feasibility?)
- Procurement sync & SOW language for customer-managed KMS + region clause: Dylan (can you prep a skeleton SOW with fallback pricing?)

I suggest we produce: 1) a one-page scope map CSV that lists in-scope services, evidence items, and owners; 2) a procurement checklist with milestone dates to match FinStack's Q3 ask.

I'll draft the scope map and send to Marta with a proposed 30-min kickoff for Thurs 11am PT. If that slot doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Marta / Evan / procurement team — thanks for the fast turn. Attached is the scope-map.csv I mentioned and a short kickoff agenda. Highlights and next steps below.

Highlights: 
- Scope confirmed: production-only for Phase 1 (api gateway, ingest-prod, ml-infer-prod).
- Region: US-only requirement noted; we'll pin hosts to us-west-2 and ensure backups remain in-region. Sean confirmed no cross-region hot backups by default (he's copied).
- KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed DEKs via our KMS integration. Sean — I flagged two technical notes in the scope map for your review.
- Evidence: We'll provide SOC2 summary + control mapping, access logs via API exports, and optional syslog pull. If FinStack prefers an agent for richer logs, that will be an add-on (see procurement checklist).

Proposed milestones (tentative):
1) This week: FinStack confirms availability for Thurs 11am PT for the technical kickoff.
2) Within 48 hours of kickoff: Redwood returns an evidence ask list and a redline-ready SOW skeleton.
3) Procurement window: target contract execution by 2026-08-20 to meet Q3 rollout planning.

Calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood-security/finstack-kickoff — please pick a time or propose an alternative.

Attachments: scope-map.csv (csv), procurement-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Questions for you, Marta: 
- Can you confirm whether their staging will be permanently excluded or if a future phase will add staging/dev? I want to call this out explicitly in the SOW.
- For logs: would an API export suffice for first-pass evidence collection? If not, which log categories require an agent?

I'll wait for confirmation of the Thurs slot and will add Daniel Ruiz if you want the economic buyer on the kickoff.
